prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Pearland, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1161; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling southbound in the left lane approaching the intersection in Pearland, Texas, when the vehicle was struck on the driver side by Driver 2, who was entering the intersection from a cross street. Driver 1 identified himself as the registered policy holder for the vehicle and confirmed he was operating it at the time. A passenger was seated in the front right seat and was also present at the scene, and witnesses at the corner independently identified that person as being inside the vehicle during the collision. Driver 1 reported pain in the left wrist and was evaluated on scene; the nature of the complaint is consistent with the force and direction of this type of impact. Driver 2 gave a statement matching the sequence described by Driver 1, and two bystanders provided accounts that agree on the signal phase and point of impact. Scene photographs show damage concentrated on the driver side door and quarter panel, which corresponds with the reported impact angle. Several light scratches on the rear bumper appear older and weathered, and may predate this incident; they were noted but not attributed to this collision. Reporting officer, unit assigned.
